Alif-Lam-Mim (1) Tanzil al-kitab ... la'allahum yahtadun (1-3)

They knew how speech is formed from these letters, and they also knew how great the difference was between the speech they themselves produced from these letters and this Book. Such an effect is not found in any words or poetry that a human being composes himself or has composed. This was a distinctive quality of the Qur'an about which no one, whether supporter or opponent, had any doubt, for whoever heard this speech felt it. He found it distinguished from other speech and was moved by it, even though he did not know that it was the Word of God. When the Qur'an was heard in Makkah even by opposing people, this element of speech affected them. Different people experienced different outcomes.

The difference between the speech and poetry of the Arabs and the chapters and verses of the Qur'an is the same as the difference between the creations of Allah and the creations of human beings. The creations of Allah are clear, distinct and separate. No human artificial thing can rival a thing made by Allah. Take the smallest thing: take a real flower and an artificial flower. If all the painters of the world were commanded to join together and produce a picture that could match the distribution of colours in a single real flower, they would not be able to do it. The colour scheme of a single flower is itself a miracle. The same is the case with the Word of Allah and other human speech, which are all made of the same alphabet.

Tanzil al-kitab la rayba fihi min rabb al-alamin (32:2) "The revelation of this Book, there is no doubt in it, is from the Lord of the worlds." This is a decisive statement, and there is no doubt that this Book is from the Lord of the worlds. The beginning of this sentence with the disjointed letters (huruf muqatta'at) is an indication that if anyone has doubts, here are the letters, the material from which this speech is made; make one too. Therefore there is no room for doubt. These letters are available to you, you are people of the language, and the style of this Book is such that you yourselves regard it as miraculous speech. This is your experience, and the common view of your experienced people.

Every chapter and every verse of this Qur'an contains within itself a miraculous element. This element is very deep within this speech, and it shows that there is a hidden power within this speech. When it is recited, a tremor comes upon a person; he is moved, he is shaken, and he loses control over himself. Whenever anyone has opened his heart to it, the sensibility has lent its ear, and human perception has been elevated, a desire to hear and accept it has arisen. As human culture, knowledge and insight expand, this distinctive quality of the Qur'an becomes increasingly prominent. As human knowledge grows, he extends his observation far across this universe, and he extends his knowledge of this universe and of its creatures and individuals. The effect of this speech is not temporary. It is a fundamental reality when the Qur'an speaks to human nature, and this effect emerges as a reality when the Qur'an addresses an experienced heart and mind, when it speaks to an educated intellect, one that speaks from a full mind, one that contains knowledge and information. As the level of a person's knowledge, culture and information rises, the meanings, concepts and effects of this Qur'an increase (provided that human nature is upright, has no crookedness, and has not had veils of base desires drawn over it), and a person comes to feel with certainty that it has been sent down by the Lord of the worlds.

Bal huwa al-haqq min rabbika (32:3) "Rather, it is the truth from your Lord." Truth: it is in accordance with the primordial nature (fitrah). It is in accordance with the truth and reality that exists within the universe. Therefore a deep truthfulness is found within it. Its structure, its exposition, the stability and permanence of its system, its being comprehensive and exclusive, the harmony of its parts without conflict or contradiction, and the mutual acquaintance and unity of its parts, all bear witness to its being the truth.

It is the truth because it creates a connection between human beings and the laws of nature that exist in this universe. There is complete harmony between the universal laws of the human being and of this universe, and the Qur'an creates concord and peace between a human being and these cosmic forces. Thus human power and cosmic powers become mutually supportive and mutually meeting, and full reconciliation exists between them. In this way a human being becomes a friend of this vast environment. This is a truth such that when human nature finds it, it responds to it, with the utmost ease, the utmost joy and the utmost eagerness, without any hardship or enmity, because the eternal and ancient truth has been placed within both.

This is a truth in which there is no contradiction and no conflict, and it is a complete way of life for all of humanity. This way has been designed with careful regard for human personality, their strength, their emotions and inclinations, their state of health and state of sickness, their state of strength and state of weakness, their state of peace and state of corruption. This is a truth in which there is complete justice. It commits no injustice either in this world or in the Hereafter, nor does it commit any injustice towards the nations that exist among human beings. It does not commit injustice towards religious and intellectual forces either. It does not oppress any human activity and thereby prevent it from a reasonable endeavour, so long as that endeavour is within the sphere of this universal truth which has been deposited in the whole of this universe.

Bal huwa al-haqq min rabbika (32:3) "Rather, it is the truth from your Lord." It is not from you; it is from the Lord. This Lord is not only the Lord of the Muslims; He is the Lord of the worlds. This is the dignity of humanity within this truth. Within it there is honour for the Messenger, for he is not fabricating anything of his own. Then it is also a colour and reflection of the closeness between Allah and the Messenger ﷺ. And this is the answer to their accusation that it is a fabrication against Allah. By "your Lord" it is intended to establish that there is a firm bond between the Prophet ﷺ and the Qur'an's source and fountainhead, the Almighty. It is an honourable bond, and because of it he conveys the revelation precisely, with great responsibility and trustworthiness.

Li tundhira qawman ataahum ... la'allahum yahtadun (32:3) "So that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that perhaps they may be guided." The Arabs, for whom the Messenger ﷺ was sent. Before him no messenger had been sent to them. History mentions no messenger from among the descendants of Isma'il, who were the forefathers of the Arabs, arriving among them. Allah sent down this Book upon Muhammad ﷺ, which is truth, the truth that is also present in human nature and in human hearts.

These people, to warn whom this Book was sent down, so that they might be warned, were associating other deities with Allah. Hence from here begins the mention of those attributes of Allah through which they may come to know what the distinctive attributes of Allah's divinity and sovereignty are, and thus they would come to know that their beliefs are extremely worthless. The subject of these great attributes is Allah, who is the Lord of the worlds, and none is worthy of being His equal or peer. Nor should they make anyone else His equal.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 32, verse 4–9 (part 1 of 2):

Allah alladhi khalaqa ... qalilan ma tashkurun (32:4–9)

This is Allah, and these are the signs and evidences of His divinity. This universe is an open book, and in its boundless expanse there are evidences that lie beyond the limited grasp of man. The creation of man himself and the various stages of his growth are known to people, and in these stages of human development, of which man is still unaware, there are evidences as well.

Allah alladhi ... sittati ayyam (32:4): "It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days." These six days are certainly different from the days we know, for the days of the earth are those that arise from the rotation of the earth on its axis in front of the sun. Such a day consists of one night and day, and this earth is a very small fragment within this universe, a mote for which there is no worth in that vast expanse. Our days and nights came into being after the creation of the heavens and the earth, and these days and nights are the measure of time by which we make our reckonings and calculations.

As for the reality of these six days, knowledge of it belongs to Allah alone. We have no means of calculating these days. They are the days of Allah, concerning which Allah said:

Fi yawmin kana miqdaruhu alfa sanatin mimma ta'udun (32:5): "And a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count." These six days may be the six conditions through which the heavens, the earth and the atmosphere between them passed until they reached their present state; or they were six stages of creation; or they were six periods, the duration between which only Allah knows. Whatever is meant, they are not the days of our time. It is an unseen matter, and we cannot specify its meaning. What is meant is the period that was spent in creation, in accordance with divine wisdom in the decree, and in that period Allah brought everything to its present form through various stages and phases.

Thumma istawa 'ala al-'arsh (32:4): "Then He istawa (rose) over the Throne." Istiwa' 'ala al-'arsh points to the fact that the whole universe is within Allah's power. As for what the Throne is, we can say nothing about it, and we stop at these words. In any case, istiwa' 'ala al-'arsh means comprehensive power. Moreover, the word thumma (then) is not for chronological sequence, because Allah's states do not change. It is not possible that Allah was in one state and then came to be in another. It is a sequence of meaning: that Allah created this universe, and from the time He created it, it has been in His power. In general it is said that creation came first and power over it afterward, but there was never a time when it was not within Allah's power. After this description of unrestricted power, people are now addressed.

Ma lakum min dunihi min waliyyin wa la shafi' (32:4): "You have no protector or intercessor besides Him." Where and who could be an intercessor when Allah, glorified is He, is established upon the Throne, the heavens and the earth are all within His power, and He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth? Who could be a protector besides Him, who could be an intercessor besides Him, and who could be an intercessor who is outside the dominion of Allah?

Afala tatadhakkarun (32:4): "Will you not then pay heed?" This truth reminds you to acknowledge Allah and to turn your face toward Him. Creation is His, He alone has complete authority, He alone manages and decides affairs, in this world and in the Hereafter. All matters of the heavens and the earth ascend to Him; on the Day of Resurrection all affairs will be presented before Him, and in this world all reports reach Him in that long day whose measure He knows.

Yudabbiru al-amra ... mimma ta'udun (32:5): "He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count."

The Qur'anic manner of expression vividly portrays the wide field of Allah's management of the universe.

Min al-sama' ila al-ard (32:5): "From the heaven to the earth." The purpose of this is to fix the matter in the human mind, that is, in words that the human mind can conceive, so that fear of God may arise in the heart. Otherwise, the scope of Allah's management of the universe is far wider than heaven and earth. But for human feeling and consciousness it is enough that one stands before this universe and imagines the breadth of Allah's management to the extent of one's own consciousness and observation. Otherwise, the truth is that the breadth of Allah's management is wider than our imagination and even wider than those calculations that are within our use.

Then, in the report of all of Allah's arrangements and all of His decrees, their results are raised up to Him, and these reports, with all their consequences and outcomes, with all deeds, possessions and actions, concerning things, living beings and all the material of the universe, are raised up on a day. The measure of that day is a thousand years according to our reckoning. In short, nothing in this universe is left to chance, nor was anything created in vain; rather, all things are managed until an appointed time. Every thing, every matter, every result and every event is under Allah, and its report reaches Allah in the manner He demands.

Dhalika 'alim al-ghaybi wa al-shahadati al-'azizu al-rahim (32:6): "That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Mighty, the Merciful." That is, this creation of the heavens and the earth, this istiwa' 'ala al-'arsh, and the management of all affairs from heaven to earth. This is Allah, the Knower of the unseen and of the observed world, the Creator. He is the absolute Power, Mighty and Merciful. He has power and can do whatever He wills. Yet in His dealings with creatures He is merciful.

Alladhi ahsana kulla shay'in khalaqahu (32:7): "He who made well everything He created." How glorious is Allah! Truly this is the truth; nature sees it, eyes see it, the heart sees it, and the intellect confirms it. This truth is in the forms of things, in their duties, in their nature and their harmony. It is in their structure and in their shape. In any case, whatever is related to beauty and excellence exists in this creation.

Subhan Allah! This is Allah's craftsmanship in all things. The marvels of His power are present in all things. Whatever Allah has made is beautiful and complete. It is neither beyond its limit nor does it have any defect. Neither more nor less than its beauty. Neither excess nor deficiency. In terms of size, in terms of shape, and from the angle of purposes and benefit. Everything is with a determined measure. Neither less nor more than the limit of beauty and grace. It does not come before its time nor after it. It does not exceed its limit nor fall behind. Beauty is observed from the smallest particle to the largest bodies. From the simple cell to the most complex living things, everything is beautiful and fitting. Likewise, deeds, conduct, events and movements are all predestined. All are Allah's creation, and every event and every occurrence follows its appointed standard and produces its determined effects, and this happens according to the plan and design that Allah prepared from eternity and will continue thus in accordance with divine management until eternity.

Every thing and every creature is created so that it may perform its determined and appointed duty, and the determination of that duty has been made with extremely precise measure. All the functions of that thing have been placed within it, and by means of these properties it performs its appointed function and is fully fit for it. After this explanation, these doubts and these objections themselves appear strange and foolish.

How this first cell comes to such quantity and abundance, then how within it division takes place according to nature, and then how from this one initial point and cell a great collection of cells comes into being. Then where the characteristics of man were hidden within those cells, and how the specific capacities arise in the embryo. How the determined duty for each cell is established, and how the characteristics of each become distinct from the others. Who would believe in the occurrence of such a miracle if this miracle were not actually coming into existence before our eyes every day?

It is the hand of the power of Allah that thus made man equal and proportioned him, and then it is the process of breathing the spirit into man by Allah that makes man into a human being. This is the only reasonable explanation of this miracle which occurs every second. Yet people are heedless of it. It is the breathing of the spirit by Allah because of which man becomes man. Within him arises the power of hearing and learning, and by this hearing and sight, man is distinguished and set apart from all other living beings.

وجعل لكم السمع والابصار والافئدة (32:9) "And He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts." This is the miracle that takes place before our eyes every second. Its explanation is nothing other than the breathing of the spirit by Allah; otherwise human intellect would keep drowning in this boundless ocean and would not be able to explain it even until the Day of Resurrection. Besides this, it is an outpouring of Allah's grace and mercy, and it is the grace of Allah alone that makes a human being from one point of this worthless water. Then it is Allah who places within this one small cell such characteristics of development and growth that it reaches the form of a human being through transformations and by acquiring further characteristics within itself, in which such qualities arise that man becomes distinguished among all other living beings. People, however, do not give thanks at all for this grace and mercy of Allah. ﴿Little is it that you give thanks.﴾ (32:9)

In light of the creation of man, his various stages, his wondrous passage through them, the constant occurrence of this great miracle, and its repeated display before our eyes, the question of how, when this man dies and becomes dust again and mixes with the other dust of the earth, resurrection and gathering will take place does not even arise. After this explanation, these doubts and these objections themselves appear strange and foolish.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 32, verse 10:

وقالوا ءاذا ضللنا ۔۔۔۔۔ ربھم کفرون (10)

These people used to say: "How can it be possible that, after we have died and been buried, and after our bodies have turned to dust and mingled with the earth, we should be brought back into existence anew, when our particles would be mixed with other particles and become non-existent and lost?" When one reflects on the first creation of man, its re-creation for Allah is nothing strange or extraordinary. In the beginning, Allah created man from clay, and this clay was from the same earth in which they wish to lose their very selves. The second creation is also like the first creation. Nothing strange or extraordinary appears in it. The real matter is this.

بل ھم بلقای ربھم کفرون (32: 10) "Rather, they deny the meeting with their Lord" (Surah As-Sajdah 32:10). For this reason they speak such things. It is the denial of appearing before Allah that causes these people to cast doubt upon such a clear matter. This is a matter that has already happened once, and such events and miracles continue to occur at every moment. The emphasis is on their death and on their return to Allah, and the evidence is the same as that which was given before this.

Qul yatawaffakum ... ila rabbikum turja'un (11): This is conveyed as a certain piece of information. Who the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is, and how he takes complete possession of human beings, is one of the unseen matters of Allah's decree. Allah has informed us that he takes people fully into his control and then will present them on the Day of Resurrection. We should believe in this and should not go into further details. (We believe) because this information has come through Allah's truthful means.

In connection with the matter of resurrection after death, about which they doubted or wished to doubt, Allah places them before one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection. This is a living and vivid scene, full of movement and dialogue, as if the event were happening right now.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 32, verses 12–14:

ولو تری اذ المجرمون ۔۔۔۔۔۔ بما کنتم تعلمون (12 – 14)

This is a scene in which the deniers of the Resurrection confess with the greatest shame. Now they accept the truth which they used to deny. They will request that they be returned to the earth, and that this time they will make up for the shortfall they committed the first time. Here, out of shame, they will stand with their heads bowed. Now these people will be "before their Lord" ('inda rabbihim), the One before whom they used to deny that they would appear. But all these statements of theirs will come too late, and now confession and declaration will benefit them nothing. Before any comment is made on their shame, it is made clear which force is decisive in this world and the Hereafter, and which is the force that decides the final end of people.

ولو شئنا لاتینا ۔۔۔۔۔ والناس اجمعین (32: 13) "Had We willed, We would certainly have given every soul its guidance, but My word has come true, that I will fill Hell with jinn and humankind together." If Allah willed, He would have placed all people on one path. This was the method of guidance, just as the way of that creation which lives according to the inspiration of nature is one, and which passes its entire life in one manner, such as insects, birds, and animals that walk upon the earth, or the creation that is obedient, such as the angels. But the requirement of Allah's will was that humans have a particular temperament and essence. It is within their power to choose guidance or to choose misguidance, and with this particular nature they play a particular role in this world for which Allah has sent them to this earth, and sent them according to a plan. Accordingly, as a requirement of that plan, Allah has decreed that He will fill Hell with jinn and humankind, namely those among the jinn and humankind who adopt the path of misguidance, a path whose end is Hell. These people who have been presented before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are the very ones who, by their own choice and pleasure, adopted the path to Hell. Now they stand before Allah with heads bowed in shame. Thus it is said:

فذوقوا بما نسیتم لقآء یومکم ھذا (32: 14) "So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day. Indeed We have forgotten you, so taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do." Now taste the consequence of your conduct, that you forgot the meeting of this Day. This is your Day, which is present, since in this scene We are seeing it present. Since you had forgotten this Day, now taste its consequence. You had ample time, but you made no preparation for it.

ان نسینکم (32: 14) "Indeed We have forgotten you." Allah does not forget anyone. But He treats them in such a way as though they have been made forgotten. This is a treatment in which they have been disregarded in a demeaning manner.

وذوقوا عذاب الخلد بما کنتم تعملون (32: 14) "Taste the punishment of eternity in recompense for what you used to do." Now the curtain falls on this scene. A decisive word is spoken, and the criminals are left in their evil end. This scene is imprinted upon the mind of the reader of the Qur'an in such a way that it is as if these people have now been left there in that very state. They stand where they were left. This is the Qur'an's inner portrayal.

Now the curtain falls on this observed scene and another scene comes into view; the atmosphere and setting of this second scene are different. It is another fragrant and refreshing atmosphere in which the heart soars. This is the scene of the believers: those who fear Allah, worship Him with complete devotion, invite people to Allah while fear of Him dwells within their hearts, whose hearts tremble. These people are full of hope in Allah's grace and favor. For them the Lord, Possessor of Majesty, has prepared what no human can even imagine.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 32, verses 15–16:

انما یؤمن بایتنا ۔۔۔۔۔ جزاء بما کانوا یعملون (15 – 17)

"So no soul knows what has been kept hidden for them of that which will delight the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do."

This is a most beautiful and luminous portrait of the people of faith. They are extremely refined, pure, and sensitive people. Their hearts tremble with fear of God, and they turn to His obedience with the greatest hope. They do not feel ashamed to worship Allah. Nor do they show arrogance or pride before Allah. Such people are in truth the ones who believe in the signs of Allah. They receive the signs of Allah with keen sensitivity, an awakened heart and an enlightened conscience. These are the people who, when the signs of Allah are recalled to them, fall down in prostration.

اذا ذکروا بھا خروا سجدا (32: 15)

﴿When they are reminded of them, they fall down prostrating﴾ (32:15). Because they are deeply affected by the signs of Allah. Hearing the words of Allah, they fall down in prostration, glorifying Allah and His signs, realising that the greatness of Allah and His signs can be expressed only by prostrating oneself, and that this expression is achieved only by placing one's forehead in the dust.

وسبحوا بحمد ربھم (32: 15)

﴿And they glorify the praises of their Lord﴾ (32:15). That is, physically they prostrate, and with their tongues they glorify (Allah).

وھم لا یستکبرون (32: 15)

﴿And they are not arrogant﴾ (32:15). Because, being obedient, turning to Allah, and conscious of Allah's greatness, they fall down in prostration. Now look at the picture of their physical form; the manner of expression is such that their inner, spiritual and mental state becomes embodied and stands before us.

تتجافی جنوبھم عن المضاجع یدعون ربھم خوفا وطمعا (32: 16)

﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾ (32:16). These people rise at night for prayer, that is, for the last prayer of 'Isha, for the witr, for the tahajjud, and for supplications at night. But the Qur'an has expressed these matters in this manner: their sides leave their beds. The image of beds at night is drawn in such a way that a person leaves that comfort, rest, sleep and other pleasures with great difficulty. But their sides, in the face of soft beds, rest, sleep and luxury, have another task. They have their work with their Lord. They are aware that they have to appear before their Lord one day, and they turn to Allah between fear and hope. The fear is of Allah's punishment and the hope is of Allah's mercy. The fear is of Allah's wrath and the hope is of Allah's pleasure. The fear is of disobedience to Allah and the hope is of the success to obey Him. The Qur'an has expressed all these matters in extremely concise words, in a most embodied manner.

یدعون ربھم خوفا وطمعا (32: 16)

﴿They call upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾ (32:16). Apart from prayer and supplication made with this sensitivity, trembling, humility and lowliness, and weeping, they are also concerned for the welfare of their society, and seeking to please Allah they pay zakat.

ومما رزقنھم ینفقون (32: 16)

﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾ (32:16). With these exalted, luminous, sensitive and compassionate souls, Allah's dealing is also most compassionate, and a most unique kind of reward is prepared for them: a reward in which special mercy shines forth. For them an announcement of a special honour is made. Allah's grace is upon them, and Allah the Exalted holds special and hidden mercies and bonds for such elevated souls.

فلما تعلم نفس ۔۔۔۔۔ کانوا یعملون (32: 17) ” “۔ This is a strange mode of expression. Allah has a hidden relationship with His servants. Allah Himself has prepared gifts for His friends; He has kept them concealed and has given no one any information about them, so that they may be revealed suddenly on the Day of Resurrection. Now, how honourable is this meeting, how eagerly awaited it is, and how magnificent it is that in it Allah will distribute among His friends unseen gifts that have already been prepared, and that Allah will distribute these gifts in His own presence.

Glory be to Allah! What bounties Allah bestows upon His servants. How He honours them with His grace and generosity. Whatever their deeds, whatever their worship, and however much their obedience may be, Allah has nevertheless prepared certain gifts for them Himself, with great care, consideration, generosity and kindness. This is the grace and bounty of Allah, and He is the Possessor of great grace and bounty.

Then the detail of this summary is given again. In comparison with the wretched end of the guilty criminals, the excellent end of the believers is stated in somewhat more detail, showing how justly Allah will reward the believers for their deeds. He will distinguish between the end of the believers and that of the criminals in both this world and the Hereafter; that is, besides the hidden gifts, their deeds will also be recompensed in full.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 32, verses 18–22:

Afaman kana mu'minan ... innā min al-mujrimīna muntaqimūn (18–22). Believers and sinners are not equal in temperament, consciousness or conduct, such that they would be equal in the reward of this world and the Hereafter. The nature of the believer is upright and sound, and he turns towards Allah. He lives according to Allah's straight path and straight system. The sinner (fāsiq) is deviant, misguided, a spreader of corruption on earth, and does not walk on Allah's straight path, nor does he live according to the Islamic system of law. Therefore it is no wonder that the believer and the sinner do not live a similar life, and that their end in this world and the Hereafter is not the same. Each of them will receive, in both this world and the Hereafter, reward and punishment according to what he has done.

Wa-mā alladhīna āmanū ... al-māwā (32:19): "As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are the gardens of refuge." They will settle in these abodes, and these abodes will embrace them. They will be good dwelling places for them, and they will remain in these stations, as a reward for their good deeds.

Wa-ammā alladhīna fasaqū fa-mā'uhumu al-nār (32:20): "And as for those who committed sin (fisq), their abode is the Fire." They will return to it, and there they will take shelter. How evil a resting place it is.

Kullamā arādū an yakhrujū minhā u'īdū fīhā (32:20): "Whenever they wish to come out of it, they will be returned into it." This is a scene full of vigorous movement: people are fleeing, and they are being seized and thrown back into Hell.

Wa-qīla lahum ... kuntum bihi tukadhdhibūn (32:20): "And it will be said to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny." This is a rebuke, to humiliate them further and to increase their punishment.

This is the end of the fāsiq people in the Hereafter. However, they are not given respite until the coming of the punishment of the Resurrection. Before the Resurrection, in this world too, they are warned with punishment.

Wa-lanudhīqannahum min al-'adhābi ... yarji'ūn (32:21): "Before that greater punishment, We will certainly make them taste a lesser punishment in this world, that perhaps they may return." 

But even within these lesser punishments, in reality the mercy of Allah is hidden. Allah does not like to punish His servants regardless, if they do not deserve punishment, if they do not persist in sins. Allah says: My minor punishment that keeps coming upon My servants is also to warn them, so that perhaps they may return, their nature may awaken, and this punishment may bring them onto the right path. And if they turn back, they will be saved from that greater punishment which has already been presented to them in the previous scene. If they were reminded of the verses of their Lord and they turned away from them, and because of this a minor punishment came upon them, and then they did not take heed and did not return from their course, then they are wrongdoers.

Wa-man aẓlamu ... a'raḍa 'anhā (32:22): "And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord and then turns away from them?" Therefore such people deserve that vengeance be taken upon them.

Innā min al-mujrimīna muntaqimūn (32:22): "Indeed, from the criminals We will take vengeance." This is a terrifying threat: Allah, the Compeller and the Proud, is issuing this warning and declaring that from such criminals I will take vengeance. In the face of Allah, what can these helpless weak ones do? How great is the vengeance of Allah!

This lesson now concludes with the end of the criminals and the righteous, the believers and the sinners. The end of both kinds of people is depicted in the form of scenes of the Resurrection, about whose occurrence these people used to doubt. After this, in the flow of the discourse, a glance is cast upon the circumstances of Prophet Musa (Moses) and his people. The Book was given to Musa so that it would be a book of guidance for the Children of Israel, just as the Qur'an was given to Muhammad (ﷺ) so that it would be guidance for the believers. The bearer of the Qur'an and the bearer of the Torah agree upon one outlook on life, and just as the followers of Musa acted with patience and steadfastness and they were made leaders of guidance, so too, if the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) act with patience and steadfastness, they too will deserve imamate. What are the qualities of the community deserving of imamate?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 32, verses 23–25:

فلا تکن فی مریۃ من لقائہ (32: 23) "So you should have no doubt about meeting it (the Book)." This is a parenthetical clause, and its meaning is that you should remain firm upon the truth that has been given to you. This is sufficient, just as it was given to Musa, and the same truth was present in the two books of these two Messengers. This explanation is better than the one given by some exegetes, that this verse alludes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ meeting Musa during the Night of Ascension (Mi'raj). In short, attaining this truth, which was also attained by Musa, is more excellent than meeting Musa, and both Messengers came together upon the same Haqq (truth) and the same reality. It is fitting to mention this here. It should be kept in mind that this refers to the hardships and trials that the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims were enduring at the hands of the opponents. The Messenger of Allah was being denied, and the disbelievers were turning away, so here it is said that you should remain steadfast, and the subsequent verses also point to this.

وجعلنا منھم ائمۃ ۔۔۔۔۔ بایتنا یوقنون (32: 24) "And when they showed patience and continued to believe in Our signs, We appointed from among them leaders who guided by Our command." Here, to the small community of believers in Makkah, a signal is given that you should be patient in the same way that the chosen believers of Musa were patient, and just as leaders were raised up from among them who ruled according to the Shari'ah of Allah, so too will there arise from among you those who will rule according to the Islamic Shari'ah, provided you are patient and certain. As for the question that the Children of Israel differed in later eras, that is left to Allah. He alone will decide regarding those differences.

ان ربک ھو بفصل ۔۔۔۔۔ یختلفون (32: 25) "Indeed, your Lord will decide between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ."

Now the context places the deniers of Makkah before the panorama of human history, so that they may look at it with a lesson-taking eye.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 32, verse 26:

أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ ۔۔۔۔۔ أَفَلَا يَسْمَعُونَ (26) The fate of the peoples destroyed in history is a lesson for all later deniers. The sunnah (way and law) of Allah operates throughout this universe, and it shows no one any favour or leniency. This humanity is subject to the divine laws of nature governing its rise and decline. The secret of its weakness and its strength lies in following or rejecting these divine laws. The Qur'an repeatedly points to the fact that Allah has established special laws for the rise and fall of nations, that these laws operate continuously, and that in past events and the ruins of destroyed nations there is a great lesson. This subject should be studied independently, so that people's hearts are awakened through the remains of the past, that they develop a sense of awareness, and that people fear Allah's seizure and retribution, for Allah has seized mighty tyrants. Moreover, historical study is necessary, because no nation can seclude itself in some corner of time and space. Nor can it ignore the system according to which the caravan of human life is moving forward, and has been moving forward continuously for centuries. Since most nations did not learn from history, they were annihilated.

The truth is that the remains of destroyed nations contain a very profound lesson, and this lesson is very frightening, provided the heart has understanding and sense and insight are present. If someone reads this lesson, a tremor overcomes the reader. The conscience trembles and the hearts are shaken. The Arabs, who were first addressed in these verses, used to see the remains of the peoples of 'Ad, Thamud and Lot spread around them. The Qur'an rebukes these people, saying that the remains of these nations lie scattered before them. You pass over them by night and by day, yet still no fear of God arises in your hearts. Your awareness is not awakened. No light of brightness appears in your feelings. And you take no measures to protect yourselves from this kind of end. You do not take guidance, and you do not adopt precautionary and preventive measures.

Inna fi dhalika la-ayat afala yasma'un (32:26): "Indeed in that are signs. Do they not hear?" They should listen to the stories of these people that the Qur'an presents, and then reflect upon their end, while day and night pass over the dwellings and ruins of these people. Before the warner's words prove true and they too are destroyed, they should come to their senses. After this scene of destruction and ruin, after this awakening of thought and feeling, after urging them to fear God and warning them, and after making their hearts tremble, they are directed to another sign, which after that frightening atmosphere presents a very pleasant scene. Behold, a dead land lies before you, scorched by drought, and We drive water toward it. Life begins to stir within it. Whereas in the accounts of earlier nations we read that Allah can also turn such green and flourishing land into barren wasteland.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 32, verse 27:

اولم یروا انا ۔۔۔۔۔ افلا یبصرون (27)

Do they not see that We drive the water to the barren land, and bring forth thereby crops from which their cattle and they themselves eat? Do they not see? ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops, of which their cattle and they themselves eat? Will they not then see?﴾ (27)

This dead, ruined land: they see that the power of God drives water towards it. Do they not see that this very dead land has become green and flourishing, full of life, and sways with abundance? Crops grow. People eat, and their cattle eat too. The scene of dead land, on which the rain falls and it becomes alive and radiant, is in truth a most effective scene for opening the closed doors of hearts. Look: life and the growth of vegetation everywhere, and the joy and welcome of people and cattle. The awareness of the sweetness and freshness of life. Then the beauty of this green life and this fresh, lovely environment: the melodies in an atmosphere of closeness and love, in which the splendour of God's power is visible everywhere, and the examples of His craftsmanship lie scattered all around, and through which, on the pages of this universe, scenes of life and beauty appear on every side.

Thus the Noble Qur'an takes the human heart on a tour of the various ups and downs of life, where there is life and growth, greenness and freshness, and also the battlefields and remains of the destruction of earlier peoples. Everywhere the Noble Qur'an strives to stir the human heart, to awaken it, and to create in it an attachment to this world. It should not pass heedlessly over this world and its varied wonders. It should remove the veils from the eyes, strive to know the secrets and mysteries of these sights and scenes of divine power, draw a lesson from events, and derive proofs and arguments from history.

Finally, after this long journey, the concluding verse of the Surah comes. It is stated that these people hasten the coming of the punishment with which they are threatened. In reality, these people regard this warning and the advice to take precautions as a doubtful matter. They are warned that the thing with which they are being threatened is true and is about to become a reality. On that day, their faith will not benefit them, and the error they have committed at that time cannot be made good. After this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told to leave them alone; they are about to reach their decisive end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 32, verse 28:

ویقولون متی ھذا ۔۔۔۔۔ وانتظ انھم منتظرون (28 – 30)

"Very well, leave them alone and wait; they too are waiting." The word fatḥ (decision, judgment) is in fact used for the decision of a dispute between two parties. The punishment with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was warning them, its coming, is also a fatḥ. These people are heedless. Allah, for some wisdom, has certainly deferred the appointed time of its coming. Even if they demand it a hundred times, Allah's affair takes place at its proper time, and when it comes, these people will be unable to resist it and will not be able to escape from it.

قل یوم الفتح ۔۔۔۔۔ ولا ھم ینظرون (32: 29) "Say: On the Day of Decision, faith will be of no benefit to those who have disbelieved, nor will they be given any respite." Whether the Day of Decision is in this world: at that time they will be seized while they are disbelievers, and then they will not be given any respite. Their faith at that time will not benefit them. And the Day of Decision will be in the Hereafter; at that time they will seek respite and it will not be granted.

This reply is numbing to the nerves, hearts tremble at it, and the final blow is dealt to them with it.

Fa-a'rid 'anhum wa-entazir innahum muntazirun (32:30) — "So turn away from them and wait; indeed they are waiting."

Beneath this sentence lies, indirectly, a hidden threat. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) shakes off his garment and leaves them to their own state, their end is known.

This final blow concludes the surah. It contains a long journey of reflection, signs and guidance, and various observations and proofs, and it seeks to affect the human heart from every side and to draw it toward guidance by attacking it from every direction.
